role: Internship, Software Engineer, Build & Simulation Platform (Winter/Spring 2027)
jd:
What To Expect
Consider before submitting an application:  

This position is expected to start around January 2027 and continue through the entire Spring term (ending approximately May 2027 or later, if available). We ask for a minimum of 12 weeks, Full - Time (40 hours/week) and on-site, for most internships. Our internship program is for students who are actively enrolled in an academic program. Recent graduates seeking employment after graduation and not returning to school should apply for full-time positions, not internships.

International Students: If your work authorization is through CPT, please consult your school on your ability to work 40 hours per week before applying. You must be able to work 40 hours per week on-site. Many students will be limited to part-time during the academic year.

About the team:

The Build and Simulation Platform team is a critical component of our vehicle firmware development process, supporting all current and future vehicle programs. Our team is responsible for building firmware packages, and then developing and maintaining simulation tooling that enables efficient and reliable testing and validation of vehicle firmware. As an intern, you will have the opportunity to tackle complex problems in distributed software and contribute to the development of cutting-edge build and simulation technologies.

What You'll Do


- Design and development simulation tooling for vehicle firmware testing and validation 
- Architecture and development of distributed build system components 
- Design and steer agentic loops for sim engine performance, cache optimization and more 
- Improve developer experience for build, test and OTA workflows 
- Work closely with the vehicle engineering teams, the users of these applications 


What You'll Bring


- Degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, or a related field of study with a graduation date between December 2026 – December 2027 
- Strong knowledge and experience in Rust, and familiarity with async Rust is nice to have 
- Experience working in a fast-paced environment on several different simultaneous projects 
- Experience with Linux Operating System internals 
- Nice to have Python, buck2 or embedded C/C++ experience 
- Nice to have Kubernetes, HPC or Docker containers experience 
- Knowledge of version control (Git) 
- Excellent interpersonal, communication, and collaboration skills 


Benefits
As a full-time Tesla Intern, you will be eligible for:

-  Medical plans > plan options with $0 payroll deduction
-  Family-building, fertility, adoption and surrogacy benefits
-  Dental (including orthodontic coverage) and vision plans. Both have an option with a $0 payroll contribution
-  Company Paid (Health Savings Account) HSA Contribution when enrolled in the High Deductible Medical Plan with HSA
-  Healthcare and Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
-  401(k), Employee Stock Purchase Plans, and other financial benefits
-  Company Paid Basic Life, AD&D, and short-term disability insurance (90 day waiting period)
-  Employee Assistance Program
-  Sick and Vacation time (Flex time for salary positions), and Paid Holidays
-  Back-up childcare and parenting support resources
-  Voluntary benefits to include: critical illness, hospital indemnity, accident insurance, theft & legal services, and pet insurance
-  Commuter benefits
-  Employee discounts and perks program
-  Earned Wage Access: Real-time pay access paid daily, subject to eligibility and schedule (applicable for below Sr. Managers levels)


Expected Compensation

$42.07 - $58.89 + benefits

Pay offered may vary depending on multiple individualized factors, including market location, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. The total compensation package for this position may also include other elements dependent on the position offered. Details of participation in these benefit plans will be provided if an employee receives an offer of employment.

jd:
What To Expect
Consider before submitting an application:  

This position is expected to start around January 2027 and continue through the entire Spring term (ending approximately May 2027 or later, if available). We ask for a minimum of 12 weeks, Full - Time (40 hours/week) and on-site, for most internships. Our internship program is for students who are actively enrolled in an academic program. Recent graduates seeking employment after graduation and not returning to school should apply for full-time positions, not internships.

International Students: If your work authorization is through CPT, please consult your school on your ability to work 40 hours per week before applying. You must be able to work 40 hours per week on-site. Many students will be limited to part-time during the academic year.

Internship Programs at Tesla

The Internship Recruiting Team is driven by the passion to recognize emerging talent. Our year-round program places the best students in positions that they will grow both technically and personally through their experience working closely with their Manager, Mentor, and team. We are dedicated to providing an experience that allows for the intern to experience life at Tesla by giving them ownership over projects that are critical to their team’s success.

What to Expect

Tesla's Software Platforms team provides the foundation on which the in-vehicle user experience is built. We own the Software Platform (kernel, bootchain, drivers, and lower-level userspace platform services) for the Infotainment systems across our vehicle lineup. This includes high resolution touch displays, high-definition audio, Bluetooth/WiFi/cellular connectivity, USB, cameras - all connected to high performance multi-core processors and GPUs. As a member of the Software Platforms Validation team, you'll be responsible for ensuring that improvements and new features for these systems in our vehicles are thoroughly vetted, building confidence and assessing risks before signing off on each software release.

Join a team of top-notch Software Engineers and Test Engineers committed to continuously improving our vehicles' features and to holding the highest bar for the performance and reliability of our software systems. You will build automation & simulation tools and fleet telemetry pipelines to perform data-based assessments of essential subsystems in our vehicles. You will collaborate across teams, HW and SW as well as Service and Manufacturing, to identify and address critical issues. The ideal candidate is a self-driven and hands-on problem solver, utilizing a range of technologies and strategies to validate and ship our software platforms.

What You'll Do


- Work on core subsystems running on the infotainment computer to perform validation reviews and risk assessments before releasing software to the fleet
- Write and ship software to the vehicle and build automated systems in the backend to generate and analyze fleet data from the millions of Tesla vehicles worldwide
- Define evaluation metrics, create visualizations and dashboards to support the monitoring and refinement of our systems
- Build and maintain HIL testers and internal frameworks/tools to accelerate experimentation and debugging of features
- Measure and optimize system performance, leveraging off-the-shelf profiling/tracing tools as well as building new custom tools
- Work cross-functionally to investigate and fix issues that you identify


What You'll Bring


- Currently pursuing a Degree in Computer Science or a related field with a gradation date between 2027 – 2028
- Proficiency with one of the following: Python, C/C++, Golang, or Java
- Experience with Linux/Unix environments & system administration, CI/CD systems, and large scale data processing & querying
- Excellent critical thinking, problem solving, and communication skills
- Experience with embedded systems software design concepts and automotive communication standards such as CAN, Ethernet, TCP/IP is a plus
- A passion for troubleshooting failures to determine root causes while constantly improving code quality & system efficiency, testability, monitoring, and observability

jd:
​ Why Ryan? 
 
• Competitively Paid Internship
 
• Award-Winning Culture
 
• Paid Holidays
 
• Mentorship Opportunities and Hands-On Training
 
• Networking with Industry Leaders
 
• All-Expense-Paid Trip to Ryan Headquarters in Dallas, TX (Summer Interns Only)

Ryan is looking for software engineering interns to help build the platform capabilities that enable development teams across the firm to deliver applications addressing our clients' needs. Our engineering teams support Tax.com, the technology engine powering Ryan's tax teams.

You will contribute to shared services, Portal experiences, reusable components, and developer tools while gaining hands-on experience with cloud solutions. Working alongside engineers and collaborating with product and design, you will learn how enterprise applications are developed, tested, secured, and delivered. You will use AI tools to accelerate learning, prototype ideas, and rapidly iterate as you contribute to a defined engineering project.

Our primary technologies are .NET and C#, React and TypeScript, and Microsoft Azure, with some exposure to Python. Duties and Responsibilities: 
 
• Develop and improve software features, shared services, reusable application components, or developer tools with guidance from experienced engineers. 
• Build and integrate APIs, shared libraries, and React single-page applications that support multiple Ryan development teams. 
• Explore Microsoft Azure services and contribute to development, testing, or deployment workflows. 
• Use AI tools to accelerate learning, prototyping, coding, and debugging; review and validate your work with the team. 
• Write automated tests, investigate defects, and participate in code reviews to improve software quality and reliability. 
• Collaborate with engineering, product, and design to understand user needs, demonstrate progress, and incorporate feedback. 
• Document what you build so other teams can understand, adopt, and maintain it. 
 Education and Experience: 
 
• Working toward a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Management Information Systems, or related study. 
• Programming coursework or experience building software through class projects, personal projects, open-source contributions, or prior work. 
• Anticipated graduation date within one year of internship 
• Minimum Overall and Major GPA of 2.8 
• Minimum of 6 – 12 Technical credit hours depending on practice 
• Tax or accounting experience is not required. 
 Professional Skills Requirements: 
 
• Strong problem-solving skills, attention to detail, curiosity, and a willingness to learn. 
• Ability to explain your work, ask questions, respond to feedback, and collaborate with teammates. 
• Ability to organize tasks, manage ambiguity, and make progress in a fast-moving engineering team. 
• Ability to work independently on a defined task and seek guidance when needed. 
 Computer Skills: 
 Basic understanding of programming and debugging is expected. Familiarity with C#/.NET, React, TypeScript, Git, APIs, automated testing, Azure, or AI development tools is helpful. Exposure to Python is a plus.

 Certificates and Licenses: 
 Valid driver's license required.

 Supervisory Responsibilities: 
 This position has no supervisory responsibilities.

 Equal Opportunity Employer: disability/veteran
